case_title: Kuna @ Sanjaya Behera v. State of Odisha
accused_victim_relationship: Relative (the accused persons are related as nephew and aunt; the co-accused appears to be the deceased's wife, but the appellant's exact relation to the deceased is not expressly stated)
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302 r/w s.34; IPC s.203 r/w s.34 (acquitted on s.203)
weapon: None mentioned for the killing (strangulation by hands); rope used to suspend the body
evidence_type: Eyewitness (sole eyewitness); medical (post-mortem); circumstantial/motive evidence; testimony of witnesses to disclosures (PW5, PW6, PW8)
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.302 r/w s.34 IPC; life imprisonment and fine of Rs. 100 (default 30 days RI); acquitted under s.203 IPC
high_court_outcome: Appeals dismissed; conviction and sentence under s.302 r/w s.34 affirmed; acquittal under s.203 affirmed on State's appeal; co-accused left free to seek premature release
neutral_facts: The victim was found hanging by a rope from the roof of a shed adjacent to the victim's house, and the victim's brother reported the death to police as unnatural. The sole eyewitness, a relative of both the victim and the accused, testified that on the night of the incident he returned from a village video show with the accused, who had been drinking. He said that when the victim was returning from relieving himself, the accused struck the victim twice from behind, sat on the victim's chest and pressed the victim's neck, while the co-accused covered the victim's mouth until the victim suffocated. He stated that the accused then tied a rope around the victim's neck and suspended the body from the shed roof, and threatened him with death if he disclosed the incident. He said the events lasted about an hour and that he raised no alarm. He disclosed the incident to three other persons about three days later. The investigating officer's spot map recorded no source of light in the locality. The post-mortem examination found death was due to asphyxia from constriction of the neck and not hanging by rope. The prosecution also relied on the victim's mother's evidence that she had rebuked the accused persons for secret talks between them. The case was initially registered as unnatural death and converted to murder six days later on the basis of disclosures by the eyewitness and three others.
physical_harm: Death of the victim by asphyxia from constriction/pressing of the neck; external injuries described as abrasions
number_of_offences: 2 charged (s.302 r/w s.34 and s.203 r/w s.34); 0 finally upheld
motive: alleged: illicit/extra-marital relationship between the accused persons; not proved by the Supreme Court, which held the High Court's inference of motive flawed
key_evidence_accepted: No evidence accepted as a sufficient basis for conviction. The Court accepted the Trial Court's analysis rejecting the motive and treated PW5, PW6 and PW8 as not substantive. The medical evidence was noted as conforming to PW1's manner of narration but was not considered safe to base a conviction on.
witness_credibility: Sole eyewitness PW1 found wholly unacceptable: related to both parties, admittedly intoxicated, silent during an hour-long incident despite 150-200 nearby residents, and unexplained delay in disclosure. PW5, PW6 and PW8 derived knowledge from PW1 and were not substantive. PW3's evidence on motive was found flawed.
post_offence_conduct: Not stated (the Court noted PW1's three-day delay in disclosure, which it found unexplained; the accused were arrested after the disclosures)
trial_duration: offence: 19/20.2.2000 (intervening night); trial judgment: 26.1.2001; High Court: 07.11.2007; Supreme Court: 17.11.2017
legal_representation: Accused (appellant): Krishnan Venugopal, Sr. Adv., with Shivendra Singh, Ms. Deepanshi Ishar, Dharmendra Kumar Sinha, Advs. State (respondent): Shibashish Misra and Ms. Sylona Mohapatra, Advs.
investigation_status: Initial report of unnatural death (20.2.2000); formal FIR registered 26.2.2000 under ss.302/203/34 IPC; inquest, spot map, seizure of rope and post-mortem done; charge-sheet filed; trial completed
procedural_irregularity: Delay in converting the case to murder (six days) and in the eyewitness's disclosure (three days); the Court treated these as weakening the prosecution case
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted s.302 r/w s.34 (life), acquitted s.203. High Court: appeals dismissed, conviction affirmed, s.203 acquittal affirmed. Supreme Court: appeal allowed, appellant acquitted.
prosecution_argument: PW1's sole eyewitness testimony is coherent and consistent and corroborated by medical evidence; PW2 and PW12 support the discovery of the body; PW1 with PW3 proves the illicit relationship as motive; delay explained by threat; Gulam Sarbar cited that ocular evidence matching medical evidence supports conviction
defence_argument: PW1's evidence is unbelievable: intoxicated, silent for an hour, no lighting shown, presence doubtful; delay in FIR and disclosure; PW5, PW6, PW8 are hearsay; injury descriptions inconsistent; illicit relationship not proved
legal_principle_applied: A conviction may rest on a single eyewitness if reliable (quality, not number, of evidence); motive is important where the case rests on circumstantial evidence; proof standard under s.3 Evidence Act (prudent man test); benefit of reasonable doubt
precedent_relied_upon: Anil Phukhan v. State of Assam (1993) 3 SCC 282; Ramji Surya Padvi v. State of Maharashtra (1983) 3 SCC 629; State of A.P. v. Patnam Anandam (2005) 9 SCC 237; Gulam Sarbar v. State of Bihar (2014) 3 SCC 401; Mahamadkhan Nathekhan v. State of Gujarat (2014) 14 SCC 589; Lokeman Shah v. State of West Bengal AIR 2001 SC 1760; M. Narsinga Rao v. State of A.P. 2001 Crl.L.J. 515 (approved); Vijayee Singh v. State of U.P. (1990) 3 SCC 190
other_sentence_order: Appellant ordered set at liberty if not required in connection with any other case
